title: Bridge the terminals the plan commons
instruction: The terminals are numbered 1 to 8 from the left end clamp. Following the terminal plan, bridge terminals 2 and 3, and terminals 5 and 6: lay one red jumper bar along the strip on top of each pair, centred over the gap between them. Bridge nothing else and leave the spare bar in the tray.
context: Panel builders common terminals with plug-in jumper bridges exactly as the terminal plan says; a bridge between the wrong neighbours shorts two circuits together, so a misplaced bridge is a wiring fault, not just a miss. The plan here is given by terminal number, so the robot has to count positions along an otherwise uniform strip. Unlike TK-7ZYLQV, where the panel's ports are numbered and listed on a card at the station, nothing marks terminals 2-3 and 5-6: the positions come only from the plan, and a stray bridge is penalised as a short. Unlike TK-PZUTS3, where one bridge goes into two named, marked test sockets, the two bridge positions must be found by counting along the strip. Done by: electrical and electronic equipment assemblers (O*NET 51-2022.00).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left), everything square to the table. Rail: a steel TS35 x 7.5 DIN rail lying flat, 3.5 cm wide, 20 cm long, 0.75 cm tall, along y, centred at x 38, y 33, fixed. On it, all fixed: a dark steel end clamp (4.5 x 1 x 3.5 cm) centred at y 41.5; eight grey terminal blocks (5.5 cm across the rail, 1.22 cm wide, 5 cm tall), 0.5 mm apart, centred at x 38 and y 40.34, 39.07, 37.8, 36.53, 35.26, 33.99, 32.72 and 31.45 (terminals 1 to 8); a second end clamp centred at y 30.29. Jumper bars: three red plastic bars 1 cm across, 2.3 cm long, 1.2 cm tall, 5 g, lying flat with their long side along y at x 24 and y 34.5, 30 and 25.5, inside a fixed white open tray (walls 0.6 cm thick, 1 cm tall, round a 6 x 14 cm pocket) centred at x 24, y 30.
scoring: From a top photo and a ruler, with the grippers open. A bar bridges a pair of neighbouring terminals when it rests still on top of the blocks (bottom within 2 mm of their top), its centre within 4 mm of the strip's centreline and within 3 mm of the midpoint between the two terminals, its long side along the strip within 8 degrees. Score: 0.5 for each plan pair bridged (2-3 and 5-6), 0.5 off for each bar resting on top of the strip anywhere else; floored at 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.5, 1.0. Success: both pairs bridged and nothing else on the strip, held 1 s.
reset_notes: Lay the three bars back in the tray on their marks.
fidelity: Rigid boxes with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). The rail lies flat on the table and the terminal strip is fixed. Real plug-in bridges push down into a jumper channel in the middle of each block and are held by their contact legs; here the bar rests on top of the blocks and is held by gravity, so bridged means lying in place, not inserted.
